title: The Day the Snowbank Blinked
skyStory: March kicks the door open like a lion with wet paws. Up above, a last quarter moon sits in Sagittarius, half lit and fully restless, flipping through a travel brochure for a place called Spring. It keeps asking if we are there yet. Saturn says no. Mars says almost. The snowbank at the end of the driveway hears all this and blinks first.

reading: The cabin chimney is puffing in short, confident bursts this morning, which is cabin language for: you have more firewood than you think. Somewhere in your week there is a task you have been treating like a mountain. It is a molehill wearing a mountain costume. Pull the costume off before noon.

At 4:40 pm a door will stick, a lid will refuse, or a zipper will jam. Do not wrestle it. Breathe out, try once more gently, and it will give. The [[Knight of Pentacles]] is slow on purpose, and today he is trying to show you that slow and stuck are not the same animal. One of them is just warming up.
joel.mission: Find the oldest pencil in the house, sharpen it, and write tomorrow's top three tasks with it in your neatest handwriting.
joel.omen: A crow standing on a snowbank like it owns the deed. It means the hard part of winter has signed its resignation.
joel.elementWhy: the snowbank is still in charge

reading: The shore has gone quiet in that grey, listening way it gets before the ice starts thinking about leaving. You are in the same mood: watching, collecting, saying very little, noticing everything. The Wood Rat files away three useful facts before lunch without even trying.

Late in the afternoon someone will tell you a story badly. They will skip the best part and lead with the ending. You will feel your hands twitch, ready to fix it. Let them finish. Then ask one question that makes them tell the good part properly, and watch their face light up like a porch lamp. That is your level-up magic, and it works on everyone.
nancy.mission: Rename one ordinary object in your home with a grand title, like The Honourable Spatula, and use the title out loud all day.
nancy.omen: A puddle shaped like a map of somewhere you have never been. It means a small adventure is already on its way.
nancy.stoneWhy: the shore is thinking about thawing

together.text: First of the month, so declare it officially. Each of you send the other a one-line weather report for March written like a pirate captain at the helm. Bonus points for the word scallywag. The best report gets pinned to the fridge of the imagination for thirty-one days.

game.intro: Monday, and the snowbank is watching. Three quick picks, ten seconds each. Saturn has the stopwatch.
